title: OpenAI ChatCompletions -> Redwood response cohesion layer (stream + tool-call mapping)
creator: Marco Silva
description: Goal: Implement a compatibility layer that maps OpenAI Chat Completions (v1) request/response semantics into Redwood's canonical inference surface while preserving streaming semantics, tool/function calling fidelity, and structured-output guarantees. This ticket covers the request-side transformations, streaming envelope mapping, incremental tool-call arg emission, and error/fallback semantics.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Redwood API can accept an OpenAI-style ChatCompletions request and produce identical observable behavior for hosted customers using openai-compatible clients (streaming + final response). 2) Tool/function calls emitted by models via OpenAI's function_call protocol are exposed to Redwood callers via our existing toolhook interface (tool invocation event + final tool result) without data loss. 3) Structured output (JSON-schema like) preserved: validation failures are surfaced with clear diagnostics. 4) Live streaming preserves chunk order/ids and can interleave assistant deltas + tool-call deltas. 5) End-to-end tests and integration playbook exist.
design_notes:
- Use a lightweight event envelope on top of our existing streaming channel to represent OpenAI choice-level semantics: {choice_id, role, delta_type, delta_payload, finished}.
- Map OpenAI 'choices' array to Redwood 'responses' stream; each choice gets a stable choice_id generated from incoming request id + choice index.
- For function calling: translate OpenAI 'function_call' incremental tokens into 'tool_call.incremental' events; on completion emit 'tool_call.completed' with parsed JSON args and run-id.
- Structured outputs: attach schema_id reference when request includes 'expected_schema' (our opt-in extension). Use streaming reassembler to validate partial JSON; if validation fails on finalization, emit a 'schema_violation' event and include best-effort parse as fallback.
- Backpressure: honor Redwood streaming backpressure; buffer a single choice's pending tool_call stream segments up to 4MB before applying slow-path persistence.
- Idempotency: include client-supplied 'oa_request_id' when present, otherwise assign 'oa_compat_id' to support retries and dedup.
tradeoffs:
- Reassembling partial JSON for structured outputs increases CPU and memory usage for high-concurrency streams; mitigated by limiting reassembly buffer per stream and providing a configurable knob.
- Preserving exact OpenAI SSE framing (event names and data blocks) is not feasible without duplicating both protocols; we instead provide a compatibility envelope that captures equivalent semantics while remaining backward compatible with Redwood streaming consumers.
- Full fidelity for nonstandard OpenAI clients (that depend on very specific chunk boundaries) is not guaranteed; we document known differences and opt to be pragmatic for the common case.
implementation_plan:
1) Prototype streaming envelope and reassembler in runtime shim (ENG branch). 2) Implement request-shaper that maps OpenAI fields (messages, n, temperature, function schemas) to Redwood request model. 3) Add tool_call event translator to tool-hook subsystem; include small runner that accepts tool invocations for local integration tests. 4) Add validation path for structured outputs and schema_violation events. 5) Integration tests: existing openai-compat e2e infra + new test vectors (streaming with toolcalls, partial JSON). 6) Docs: compatibility notes page and migration checklist for customers.
Links: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/oa-cc-compatibility+cohesion, prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7421
risks_and_blockers:
- Blocking: runtime kernel lacks safe memory accounting for per-stream reassembly under high throughput (runtime issue filed with infra).
- Risk: Some models emit malformed JSON in function args; we need robust recovery and clear signals to customers.
- Dependency on ENG-412358 for canonical streaming primitives and ENG-95321 for telemetry contract changes.
- Operational: increased metric cardinality (choice_id dimension) may spike TSDB ingestion; ops must validate retention policy before roll-out.
test_plan:
- Unit: mapping functions for request fields and function schema conversion.
- Integration: Simulate OpenAI client streaming with interleaved assistant deltas and function_call deltas; assert event order and choice_id stability.
- E2E: Deploy to staging dedicated pool, run client compatibility harness (open-source test vectors) and run canary traffic for 48h.
- Chaos: inject partial TCP disconnects to validate resume/dedup using oa_compat_id.
